## Final hypothesis

Summed social capital (Copper&Gold + Amber + Monument Count, in Z-scores) peaked in the **14th–13th century BCE (1400–1300 BCE)** — the two adjacent 100-year bins (1400 and 1300 BCE) tie at a summed Z of **4.238**, clearly above the next-highest bins (1200/1100 BCE at 3.622 and 2700 BCE at 2.959). The rise into the peak was driven primarily by **Copper&Gold (ZCU_AU), which jumped from −0.36 to +2.54 (Δ +2.90) between the 1500 and 1400 BCE bins** — a step up from its near-flat pre-peak baseline (−0.6 to −0.36 over 4300–1500 BCE) and close to its all-time maximum (2.85 in the following 1200/1100 BCE bins) — and by **Monument Count (ZMonument), which rose from +0.165 to +1.708 (Δ +1.54)** in the same transition (though its all-time maximum of 3.949 occurred earlier, at 2700 BCE). **Amber (Zamber) was roughly flat**, moving only from −0.15 to −0.01 (Δ +0.14), so it contributed little to the peak. In short: the late-2nd-millennium BCE (14th–13th c. BCE) social-capital peak was a gold/copper- and monument-count-driven phenomenon, with amber essentially unchanged.

## Workflow description

1. Parsed `capital.csv` (39 rows, BCE 4300→500, exact 100-year bins; comma-decimal values), verifying parsed numbers against raw CSV strings (4 spot checks passed); confirmed 0 NaN in ZCU_AU, Zamber, ZMonument.
2. Computed summed social capital = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument per 100-year bin; located the maximum: 4.2381, a 2-bin tie at 1400 and 1300 BCE.
3. Computed per-component deltas 1500→1400 BCE (CopperGold +2.90, MonumentCount +1.54, Amber +0.14) and full-range trends (CopperGold step-up from flat baseline, max 2.85 at 1200/1100 BCE; MonumentCount max 3.949 at 2700 BCE; Amber max 1.54 at 3300–3000 BCE).
4. Cross-checked against `time_series_data.csv` raw rows (CE=−X ↔ BCE=X): 37 overlapping bins, 0 mismatches; its summed series peaks at the identical 4.2381 in the same two bins.
5. Robustness: including MonumentSize (ZMW) still places the peak at 1400 BCE (4.904); the pollen/openness dataset contains no social-capital columns and plays no role. Executed script: `analysis.py`.

## Limitations

- The peak is a 2-bin tie, so "which century" is best stated as 14th–13th c. BCE; underlying values are period-constant (coarser than 100 years), so within-century resolution is not meaningful.
- ZMW (MonumentSize) excluded per the "monument count" definition; included only as a robustness check (peak location unchanged).
- All analysis is in Z-score space, so the peak reflects relative (standardized) abundance, not raw quantities.
